banners.cannotPlay: Clips cannot play inside this window.
banners.notRecordingHelp: Vice keeps retrying on its own. If it is an encoder problem, a reboot after a driver update usually clears it, or pick a different encoder under Settings, Recording.
banners.cpuFallbackHelp: Your GPU encoder would not open, so Vice fell back to CPU encoding to keep clipping. That costs frames in games. This is usually a driver that needs a reboot after an update. Vice tries the GPU first every time it starts, so once that is sorted this goes away on its own.
banners.codecFallbackHelp: Your GPU would not encode the codec picked under Settings, Recording, so gpu-screen-recorder chose one it can handle. Recording is still on the GPU and clips are unaffected. Choosing a different encoder yourself stops this notice, and H.264 in particular tops out at 4096 pixels wide on NVIDIA, so HEVC or AV1 is the one to pick on a wide monitor.
banners.cannotPlayHelp: The installed Qt WebEngine build has no H.264 decoder. Recording still works, and clips open fine in your system player. To fix in-app playback, install your distro's WebEngine package and reinstall Vice:
banners.cpuFallbackNvencApi: Your NVIDIA driver supports NVENC {driver}, but the FFmpeg on this system needs {required}, so the GPU encoder cannot open. That costs frames in games, and a reboot will not fix it. Recording on the GPU again needs a newer NVIDIA driver, or an FFmpeg built for NVENC {driver} if your card does not get newer drivers.
banners.nvencUseFlatpak: The Flatpak gpu-screen-recorder is installed and works with this driver: choose it under Settings, Recording.
banners.nvencGetFlatpak: The Flatpak gpu-screen-recorder works with this driver. Install it with {command}, then choose it under Settings, Recording.

tutorial.startClipping: Start clipping, then let Vice run
tutorial.colourBody: Vice takes its colour from one of these. The whole window changes as you pick, so choose the one you want to look at, and change it any time in Settings.
tutorial.quickStartBody: Vice keeps the buffer live in the background and opens this window only when you need it.
tutorial.playlistsBody: Every clip can live in any number of playlists, and they keep themselves in order.
tutorial.sessionHelp: Double-tap to start or stop a full recording. Tap once during a session to mark a highlight.
tutorial.reviewHelp: Open any clip to rename it, trim the best moment, share a link, or press H to add highlights.
tutorial.backgroundHelp: Minimize or close this window and Vice keeps recording. Discord Rich Presence is on by default and lives in Settings.
tutorial.autoHelp: Clips are filed under the game you were playing when you saved them. Vice builds these on its own.
tutorial.customHelp: Create your own from the sidebar, pick an emoji and a colour, then drag clips onto it or right-click a clip to add it.
tutorial.safeHelp: Playlists follow clips through renames and trims, and tidy up after deletions.
tutorial.bufferTitle: How far back Vice can reach
tutorial.bufferBody: Vice is always recording into a buffer it throws away. Pressing the clip key keeps the last stretch of it, and this is how long that stretch is.
tutorial.bufferNote: The buffer holds {buffer} at a time. A longer one costs memory, and Settings has the whole picture, including writing it to disk instead.
tutorial.screenshotKeyNote: The screenshot key is unset until you set one. It saves a picture of the screen to the Images section and puts it on your clipboard.
tutorial.editorHelp: Put several clips on a timeline, cut them together, add text and transitions, and export one video. It is in the sidebar.
tutorial.shareBody: Every clip has a link, and copying it is one button on the card.
tutorial.linkHelp: The link button on a clip copies an address that plays the clip in a browser. Paste it into Discord and it embeds.
tutorial.tunnelHelp: On its own the link only works on this machine. Turn on the Cloudflare tunnel in Settings and it works anywhere, until the daemon restarts and the address changes.
tutorial.moreBody: That is everything you need. Settings has the parts you only touch once.
tutorial.recHelp: Encoder, resolution, frame rate, which monitor, and which audio goes on which track.
tutorial.gameCaptureHelp: Game Capture records just the game's window, so Discord and other windows stay out of your clips. Off records the whole display. You can switch it any time from quick settings.
tutorial.shareDiscordHelp: Off, the Share button copies a link. On, it copies the clip itself, shrunk to fit Discord's free upload limit. Right-click Share for the other one, and change it any time in Settings.

accents.customBody: Pick any colour and Vice builds a full Material 3 scheme from it. Only the hue carries over: the surfaces, the buttons and the text tones are worked out from it, the same way the five presets are.
accents.lowContrast: This colour does not leave enough contrast to read comfortably. Vice has lightened the accent as far as it can; try something less dark.

settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: Tune Vice to the way you play
settings.bufferOnDisk: Buffer is kept on disk, so long durations are fine.
settings.bufferPlain: Seconds of gameplay kept in the rolling buffer
settings.bufferRamWarning: A {length} buffer in RAM uses roughly {gb} GB at typical bitrates. Auto storage moves it to disk.
settings.replayStorageHelp: Where the rolling buffer lives. Auto keeps short buffers in RAM and moves anything over ten minutes to disk.
settings.clipDurationHelp: Seconds saved when you press the clip key
settings.gsrSourceHelp: The Flatpak build carries its own FFmpeg, which still records on the GPU with older NVIDIA drivers that your system's FFmpeg no longer supports.
settings.keyOverlayHelp: Shows the keys you press in a small panel over your game, so they are in your recording and your stream. Only the keys on the panel are read.
settings.keyOverlayPositionHelp: Pick a corner, or press Move it and drag the panel where you want it.
settings.keyOverlayLayoutHelp: Labels the overlay's keys for your keyboard. AZERTY shows ZQSD where QWERTY shows WASD. The same physical keys light up either way.
settings.keyOverlayKeyHelp: Shows or hides the overlay without opening Vice.
settings.keyOverlayKeyNow: {key} now shows and hides the overlay
settings.keyOverlayInClipsHelp: Saves which of the overlay's keys you pressed during each clip, so the viewer can show them later even if the overlay was off. Nothing else you type is kept.
settings.errSaveOverlay: Could not save the overlay setting
settings.overlayNoLayerShell: Your desktop cannot keep a window above games. It works on KDE Plasma, Hyprland, Sway, Niri and X11, but not on GNOME under Wayland.
settings.overlayNoGtk: The overlay needs GTK 3 and gtk-layer-shell for Python. On Arch install gtk-layer-shell and python-gobject; on Debian and Ubuntu gir1.2-gtklayershell-0.1 and python3-gi-cairo.
settings.overlayNoDisplay: Vice could not find your desktop session to show the overlay on.
settings.overlayCrashed: The overlay keeps closing. vice.log has the reason.
settings.typeExact: {label}: click to type an exact number of seconds
settings.customResolutionWarn: Write it as width by height, like 1600x900.
settings.badResolutionTitle: That resolution is not a size
settings.badResolutionDetail: Write it as width by height, like 1600x900
settings.containerHelp: MKV survives crashes better and suits multi-track audio. Discord embeds and browsers need MP4.
settings.encoderHelp: GPU encoders are faster and use less CPU. Vulkan options require the gpu-screen-recorder backend.
settings.colourDepthHelp: 8-bit suits every player. 10-bit needs an HEVC or AV1 encoder.
settings.hardwareDecodeHelp: Let your GPU decode clips in this window instead of the CPU. Worth turning on if high-resolution AV1 or HEVC previews stutter. It renders video black on some drivers, so if that happens turn it back off. Takes effect next time you open Vice.
settings.followMouseHelp: Record whichever monitor the pointer is on. Switching monitors restarts the buffer, so a clip taken right after moving will be short.
settings.followMouseUnsupported: Needs X11, Hyprland or Sway. Vice cannot tell where the pointer is on this session.
settings.windowCaptureHelp: Record only the focused game's window instead of the whole display. Only windows Vice recognizes as a game count, so alt-tabbing to Discord or a browser does not move the capture. Switching to a different game restarts the buffer, so a clip taken right after is short.
settings.displayMissing: Display "{id}" is not being reported right now. It is still saved and will be used if it comes back.
settings.displayNone: No individual displays were detected. Auto will still work.
settings.displayHelp: Choose which display to record. Auto follows the backend default.
settings.captureMicHelp: Record your mic into clips. The same switch as the tile on Home, and saved the moment you flip it.
settings.errMic: Could not change the microphone setting
settings.desktopSourceIsMic: This is a microphone input, so clips would have no desktop audio. Pick one under Desktop audio instead.
settings.desktopSourceMissing: That source is not listed right now. It is still saved and will be passed to the recorder.
settings.desktopSourceHelp: Choose what the recorder captures as desktop audio.
settings.micSourceHelp: Used when mic capture is on. Default input follows the system setting.
settings.micMonoHelp: Centres your mic in the clip. Turn this on if your voice only comes out of one ear, which is what most XLR and single-channel interfaces do. Applied when the clip is saved, so it needs mic capture on and no separate audio tracks.
settings.desktopVolumeHelp: Balanced into new clips as they are saved
settings.micVolumeHelp: Turn this down if your mic overpowers the game. Applies while mic capture is on.
settings.notifyVolumeHelp: The ping when a clip is saved, and the session start, stop and highlight tones.
settings.customSoundsHelp: Play your own file instead of the built-in tone. Leave blank for the tone. A path that does not exist falls back to the tone, so you never end up with silence.
settings.audioTracksHelp: Each source becomes its own track for editing. Players, Discord and share links use track 1. With mic capture on, your microphone gets its own track.
settings.duplicateTrack: That source is already a track
settings.mixFirstTrackHelp: Record an extra track 1 that mixes every source, so players and shared clips carry full audio. Your separate tracks start at 2.
settings.wfMicModeHelp: How wf-recorder handles desktop audio together with a microphone
settings.wfMicTitle: How should the microphone be mixed in?
settings.wfMicBody: wf-recorder records one audio source at a time. Choose what happens when both the desktop and the microphone are on.
settings.wfMicChoiceBoth: Use a backend that can do both
settings.wfMicChoiceBothBody: Vice records with a compatible backend whenever the microphone is on.
settings.wfMicChoiceMicBody: Desktop audio is dropped while the microphone is on.
settings.clipKeyHelp: Click to rebind, then press a key or a combo like Alt+F9. Escape cancels. Saved the moment you press it.
settings.hotkeysUnavailable: Vice cannot read your keyboard right now, so no hotkey will fire. Adding your user to the input group and logging back in usually fixes it.
settings.keyUnsupported: That key cannot be bound, try another
settings.errSaveKey: The key was captured but not saved
settings.clipPresetsHelp: Each key saves its own clip length. Double-tap any clip key to start or stop a session.
settings.blocklistHelp: One per line. Vice leaves its keys alone while a matching app is focused, for games that clip on the same keys. Matched against the window process and class, for example ggst.exe. Needs X11, Hyprland, Sway or Niri.
settings.tagWithGameHelp: Append the detected game to clip filenames, like Vice_Clip_4_Overwatch-2.mp4. Uses the same game list as Rich Presence and the auto playlists.
settings.autoPlaylistHelp: When a known game is focused, file the clip into an auto playlist for it with its own colour.
settings.clipFilenameEmpty: That template renders to nothing, so the default naming will be used.
settings.portHelp: Port for the local share server
settings.publicLinkHelp: Share links that work outside your own network. Needs the cloudflared binary installed, otherwise links only work on your network.
settings.discordClientIdHelp: Optional. Leave empty to use Vice's own Discord application, or provide your own Application ID for custom branding.
settings.accentHelp: Tints the controls, the highlights and the ambient wash behind the app. Saved straight away, and shared clips pick it up too.
settings.effectsHelp: Motion and depth cost a GPU. Auto measures how fast frames arrive in this window and turns them down when it cannot keep up.
settings.effectsSoftware: This window is compositing in software, so effects are reduced.
settings.effectsSlow: Frames are arriving too slowly here, so effects are reduced.
settings.effectsKeepingUp: Frames are keeping up, so the full treatment is on.
settings.checkForUpdatesHelp: Ask GitHub once a day whether a newer Vice is out. Nothing about you or your clips is sent.
settings.checkNowHelp: Look straight away, ignoring the daily wait.
settings.upToDate: You are on the latest release
settings.bufferRaised: Buffer raised to {length} to cover your longest clip key
settings.restartBody: The sharing settings are saved, but the server only picks up a new port or tunnel setting when the daemon restarts.
settings.clipFilenameHelp: Leave empty for the default Vice_Clip_4 naming. Use {n} for the clip number, {date}, {time}, and {game} (needs the toggle above). Clips are never overwritten.
settings.discordEnabledHelp: Puts "Clipping <Game> with Vice" on your Discord profile while a known game is focused. On by default, and window titles are never sent.
settings.discordGameIconsHelp: Shows the game's own Discord icon on your profile, with Vice's logo as a small badge. Vice looks the game up in Discord's public list of detectable games and caches the result. Off, or if a lookup fails, shows the plain Vice logo.
settings.discordCustomGamesHelp: One game per line: {format}. Matches are case-insensitive substrings checked against the focused window's process name and class. The bundled list already covers over 300 games.
settings.gsrArgsHelp: Appended to the recorder command as written. Example: {example}
settings.languageHelp: Vice is translated by the people who use it. If yours is missing or half done, the file to fill in is one JSON file: see docs/TRANSLATING.md.
settings.screenshotKeyHelp: Saves what is on screen as a picture, in the Images section. Unset by default. Screenshots are copied to the clipboard as well.
settings.imageDirectoryHelp: Where screenshots are written. Kept apart from clips so an image viewer is not indexing a folder of video files.
settings.shareDiscordFileHelp: On: the Share button copies the clip itself, shrunk to fit Discord's free upload limit, ready to paste into a message. Off: it copies the share link. Right-click Share for the other one either way.

whatsNew.title: What's new in Vice {version}
whatsNew.thanks: Thanks to {names} for their work on this release.

gameCapture.title: Record only the game
gameCapture.body: Turn on Game Capture in quick settings and Vice records just the game's window, so Discord and everything else stay out of your clips. It is off unless you turn it on.

discordShare.title: Share straight to Discord
discordShare.body: Right-click Share for a copy of the clip that fits Discord's free upload limit, ready to drag or paste. Settings, Sharing can make that what Share does. The editor can also export a Discord-sized file.

tray.title: Vice in the system tray
tray.body: On desktops with a system tray, closing the window now tucks Vice into the tray instead, and clicking the icon brings it back. Quit Vice from the tray menu stops recording too.

gameIcons.title: Your game's icon on Discord
gameIcons.body: Your Discord profile now shows the game's own icon while you play, with Vice's logo as a small badge. Turn it off in Settings, Discord.

steamNames.title: More games recognized
steamNames.body: Any game installed through Steam is now named in clips and on Discord, even when it is not on Vice's own list.

keyOverlay.title: Show your keys on screen
keyOverlay.body: A keyboard overlay shows the keys you press over your game, for streams and clips. Drag it where you want it or pick a corner. Vice can also keep the keys with each clip, to show in the viewer or add to an editor export. Both are off until you turn them on under Settings, Overlay.

trimCopy.title: Trimming keeps the original
trimCopy.body: Trim now saves your selection as a new clip and leaves the recording alone. Replacing the original is still there, and asks first.

trackVolume.title: A volume for each audio track
trackVolume.body: With separate audio tracks, each one now has its own volume under Settings, Audio, so a call or your mic can be heard over the game.

niri.title: Niri support
niri.body: Vice now sees which game you are playing on Niri, for clip names, game playlists and Discord.

flatpakGsr.title: The Flatpak gpu-screen-recorder
flatpakGsr.body: Vice can use the Flatpak build of gpu-screen-recorder, which keeps recording on the GPU on older NVIDIA cards that your system's FFmpeg has left behind. Choose it under Settings, Recording once it is installed.

languages.title: French, German and Brazilian Portuguese
languages.body: Vice is now available in French, German and Brazilian Portuguese. Pick a language in Settings, Appearance.
